answer: An opal-tier identity probe inserts a unique micro-rotating optical signature into each agent's credential, so duplicated identities reveal identical wear patterns under cross-polarized light. Any delta between a claimed new agent and a previously logged signature flags a clone, forcing attackers to forge distinct, physically consistent signatures per sybil at steep cost. This nebula-wide check breaks when attackers capture genuine unused signatures, so rotation cadence and audit depth cap its reach.
